Amazon's Plan to Index the World's Online Shopping Data

Amazon's Plan to Index the World's Online Shopping Data (yahoo.com)
			
		 	
				Amazon is considering a "World Product Graph" that would index information about products sold across the internet in an effort to keep shoppers and AI agents from turning to Google, Reddit or other sources for product research. The proposed database could also improve Amazon's AI shopping assistant by addressing inaccurate or incomplete answers and allowing it to use cheaper models.
"Amazon cannot be the go-destination for every shopping mission if customers must leave to research product relationships on Google, brand websites, and review sites," according to an internal Amazon document. "These answers exist, but the only way to find them has been to leave Amazon for painstaking research on brand websites, third party review sites and tech forums." Reuters could not determine if or when this plan may be implemented, though the document, written like a press release, has an aspirational future release date of October 1, 2027.
Amazon said in a statement: "Draft, outdated documents often paint an incomplete picture and the existence of a brainstorming document such as this one doesn't necessarily reflect our current plans. We're constantly working on new ideas and technologies to make Amazon's product catalog comprehensive, accurate, and helpful for customers."

Israeli airstrike on Nasser hospital in Gaza killed surgeon and others
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-11-14
05:31:44 UTC
14:31:44 KST

An Israeli airstrike on Nasser hospital in southern Gaza killed six people, including a surgeon and a disabled man, and wounded 28 others, according to the hospital director.
The Israeli military carried out the attack on the hospital, in Khan Younis, early on Thursday saying in a statement it had struck a Hamas commander and other fighters there, without providing evidence.
The strike destroyed part of the surgery department, and caused extensive damage to several floors. Services were suspended in four departments: radiology, laboratories, surgical operations and inpatient surgical wards, according to Dr Ahmed al-Fara, hospital director.
The ceiling of one of the wards had caved in, while debris-covered beds lay next to medical instruments twisted from the force of the blast. In other rooms, piles of rubble and shattered concrete cluttered the floor and a hole was left in the floor, where the bomb penetrated the building.
Dr Ayman Abu Ubaid, a surgical specialist at Nasser medical complex, who was wounded in the attack, said: “The bombing caused thick smoke to fill the rooms and fires to break out, amid the groans of wounded and people’s screams. There were many casualties and blood everywhere … Most of us sustained injuries to our limbs, as well as shrapnel wounds in different parts of our bodies.”
Ubaid said the strike came at about 12.30am, without warning. “The patients in the department were all surgical patients waiting to undergo operations. The bombing happened at a time when they should have been asleep,” he said.
Among the dead was Rizk Abu Shaira, 52, a general surgeon who had featured in American Doctor, a documentary about doctors operating in Gaza.
“Dr Rizk was in the American Doctor documentary operating and serving his people. He lost his life doing that, he lost his life because he was doing that,” Dr Thaer Ahmad, who also featured in the documentary, posted on X.
Abu Shaira was killed alongside one of his patients, on whom he had operated.
Nasser hospital is one of the last functioning healthcare facilities in Gaza, after Israeli bombing made most of the strip’s facilities unusable. Last year Israel also struck the hospital, killing five journalists in a double-tap strike on a location often used by reporters for filming. In all, the hospital has been attacked seven times since the war on Gaza began.
The Israeli military has accused Hamas of using hospitals as command centres and to store weapons, an accusation the militant movement rejects. More than 1,700 healthcare workers have been killed in Gaza, while Doctors Without Borders (MSF) says Israel has detained hundreds of medics since 7 October 2023, with at least 95 still in custody.
About 90% of Gaza’s health infrastructure has been destroyed or damage by Israeli bombing, systematic destruction UN experts called “medicide”.
Attacking healthcare facilities and staff is illegal under international humanitarian law, though these facilities can lose their protected status if they are used for military purposes.
There is an increased need for healthcare during the winter months in Gaza, where rains have displaced people from their tents and increased communicable diseases in crowded encampments.
Already, Nasser hospital is lacking about 80% of its essential medicines and medical supplies, said al-Fara, its director.
One of those killed in Thursday’s strike was Seif Ghazi Abu Hatab, 29, who was admitted to Nasser hospital on Monday after a piece of debris fell on his back while he was helping clear rubble from a friend’s home. He was scheduled for surgery at 10am on Thursday, and was meant to receive further treatment abroad.
“Seif was a young man in the prime of his life. He wanted to live, rebuild his home and start a normal life, free from problems and suffering … Seif was killed after already losing two of his brothers and his father. His mother has now lost three of her sons,” said his cousin Tareq Abu Hatab, 37.
Israel launched the war in Gaza after the 7 October 2023 Hamas-led attack that killed about 1,200 people and took 251 hostage. At least 74,645 people have since been killed in Gaza and Israel has carried out a genocide in the strip, according to the UN independent international commission of inquiry on the occupied Palestinian territory.
Israel continues to carry out airstrikes in Gaza, killing more than 1,600 people since the October 2025 “ceasefire”, according to the Gaza ministry of health.

Run Cloudflare Workers Anywhere

Run Cloudflare Workers anywhere.
- AWS
- Google Cloud
- Azure
- Rivet Cloud
- Your servers
The same developer experience, without the runtime limits, for a fraction of the bill.
Built for serious scale.
Run it where you want.
Next to your database, in the cloud and region you choose.
Same work. A fraction of the bill.
Cloudflare's meters, priced on raw AWS.
- 4.8×
- 8.7×
- 5.7×
No runtime limits.
128 MB is all the memory a Cloudflare Worker gets. OpenOrange runs your Workers and Durable Objects on machines you choose, so the limits are your hardware's.
Don't sacrifice your DX.
Your wrangler.jsoncBindings, environments, build commands and .dev.vars work as they do with Wrangler. stays the source of truth. Same commands, new name.
Get started.
Run this project's Cloudflare Worker on Rivet with OpenOrange. First, ask me where it should run: on my machine, on a Rivet cluster, or on my own Rivet Engine. Then read https://github.com/rivet-dev/open-orange/blob/main/README.md and follow its quickstart. Do not change my app code.
- Step 1: Install Install the orange CLI globally, then run it in your Worker project. Your code and your Wrangler configuration do not change.
$ pnpm add -g open-orange
- Step 2: Run your Worker Reads your Wrangler configuration. Each Durable Object runs as a Rivet Actor with its own SQLite database. $ orange dev ● Ready in 0.9s Local http://127.0.0.1:8787
- Step 3: Deploy Builds an image of your Worker and rolls it out to your own cloud (AWS, GCP, Azure) or on-prem servers. Or use Rivet Cloud: a fully managed, dedicated cluster on AWS or Google Cloud, in the region you choose. $ orange login $ orange link --cluster <name> $ orange deploy ✓ Deployed my-worker URL https://api.example.com
Migrate your data without downtime.
orange migrate copies every Durable Object and D1*Cloudflare doesn't provide a way to migrate D1 live, so requests to a D1 database are interrupted while its data copies. This takes a few minutes. database from Cloudflare while your app keeps serving. No maintenance window, no lost writes.
Supported bindings.
Every Cloudflare binding OpenOrange runs, plus the fetch handler and runtime globals. Each is documented with its status, configuration and known differences from Cloudflare.
Questions.
Wait, wasn't Cloudflare supposed to be cheaper?
For small, spiky Workers, it often is: the free tier and per-request pricing are hard to beat. The meters add up once Durable Objects stay busy. Duration is billed per GB-second while an object is active, and every SQLite row written costs $1 per million. The same GB-hours on Graviton EC2 cost about a fifth as much, and writes cost a fraction of that.
Is OpenOrange a fork of Cloudflare?
No. OpenOrange implements the Workers API on Node.js and maps each Cloudflare service onto Rivet. It uses Wrangler to read your configuration, and it reuses some MIT-licensed Cloudflare code, such as the Workflows engine. It does not run workerd.
Why not just run workerd directly?
workerd is Cloudflare's runtime, not its platform. It runs your fetch handler, but KV, D1, R2, Queues, Workflows and the Cache API are bindings that call services you have to build, and Durable Objects keep their data on one machine with nothing to place, replicate or scale them. It also keeps limits designed around Cloudflare's network rather than your servers: only the nodejs_compat subset of Node.js, no native npm modules, and alarms capped at 15 minutes. OpenOrange runs your Worker on Node.js with real SQLite, and Rivet provides the services, so your code keeps working on infrastructure you control. Compare OpenOrange and workerd
Do I need to learn Rivet?
No. Rivet is the control plane underneath. You use the orange CLI and your Wrangler configuration.
What does it cost?
OpenOrange is Apache 2.0 and free. Self-host Rivet and your cloud bill is the only bill. Rivet Cloud and BYOC pricing is at rivet.dev/pricing.
What happens to the data already in KV, Durable Objects and R2?
orange migrate moves Durable Objects while your app serves, with no downtime. D1 databases are interrupted for a few minutes while they copy, because Cloudflare doesn't provide a way to migrate D1 live. R2 is S3-compatible, so rclone or aws s3 sync moves buckets.
Does it run at the edge?
It runs wherever you deploy it, in as many regions as you want. Most backends talk to one database; running next to it is faster than running at the edge. For stateless Worker requests, this works fine today. For Durable Objects, an upcoming Rivet update adds multi-region support, including edge regions.
Who maintains OpenOrange?
Rivet. OpenOrange is not affiliated with or endorsed by Cloudflare, Inc.
Keep the platform. Lose the walls.
Your Cloudflare project in your datacenter.
Built for serious scale.

Windows 0-Day Dropped By Disgruntled Researcher Hands Hackers System Rights
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-11-14
03:30:00 UTC
12:30:00 KST

Windows 0-Day Dropped By Disgruntled Researcher Hands Hackers System Rights (arstechnica.com) 11
			
		 	
				An anonymous reader quotes a report from Ars Technica: Nightmare Eclipse, the pseudonym of a researcher with an ongoing, very public beef with Microsoft, has dropped yet another Windows zero-day. On Tuesday, Nightmare Eclipse disclosed SignDrop, a vulnerability that gives local users full System rights on some versions of Windows. The vulnerability resides in the Common Log File System, which Microsoft describes as a "general-purpose logging service used by software clients running in user-mode or kernel-mode." By forcing a privileged process such as Windows Defender to open a crafted CLFS container, an attacker with ordinary user rights can abuse the privileged file creation to elevate privileges to System.
[...] Researcher Will Dormann said in an interview that he has been able to reproduce the exploit and that it works as described, but not on all versions of Windows 11. But there's a catch, he said. "The requirements are important in that it seems to require Windows 26H2, and one that has existed for more than 90 days, it seems," he explained. "That is, you can't just take a new 26H2 system and install updates and have it work." For a system to be vulnerable, Dormann said, the HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\CLFS\Authentication\Mode
value must be 0 or 1." Of the many machines Dormann uses, only a single one met this requirement. Microsoft said in a statement that it was investigating the vulnerability and had no evidence it was being exploited in the wild. The company also said Defender blocks potential exploitation attempts.

Nvidia Allegedly Engineered Scarcity by Funding AI Startups to Buy Its GPUs
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-11-14
02:52:59 UTC
11:52:59 KST

Friday, November 13th 2026
NVIDIA Allegedly Engineered Scarcity By Funding AI Startups To Buy Its GPUs
Following the departure of now-former NVIDIA CEO, Jensen Huang, a new report by The Wall Street Journal (via Wccftech) has emerged alleging that NVIDIA artificially inflated the ongoing GPU and memory shortage by investing in AI startups that would go on to buy NVIDIA GPUs and build data centers. The reason behind this was to maintain the perception of ongoing high demand and to move an oversupply of semiconductors from TSMC. 
The WSJ report cites an August meeting between Huang and his senior finance team, including NVIDIA's CFO and acting CEO, Colette Kress, during which Kress pushed for a reduction in circular financing agreements, in response to which Huang allegedly lay into Kress, calling her a "deer in the headlights," after she had pushed to scale back NVIDIA's $250 billion deal with OpenAI. Jensen's push for further investment into small-scale cloud providers was seemingly in response to the changing tide that saw AI hyperscalers move away from off-the-shelf components in favor of custom solutions.The situation described in the report saw NVIDIA on the hook for an "avalanche" of GPUs from TSMC, for which it would have no immediate buyers. Part of the issue highlighted by Kress was also that these small-scale cloud providers NVIDIA was investing in could not afford to buy NVIDIA GPUs, meaning they, too, could be a financial dead end.
Sources:
				The Wall Street Journal, 				via Wccftech

Ggml v1.0.0
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-11-14
02:28:29 UTC
11:28:29 KST

Repository navigation
Overview
ggml 1.0.0 prunes the deprecated public API and the legacy DIAG_MASK ops, adds configurable YaRN truncation and FP8 support, and brings broad performance work across backends: few-row quantized matmuls and MoE fusion on CUDA/Metal, a Vulkan prefill FlashAttention path, a device-side MoE scheduler on SYCL, decomposed Adreno FlashAttention in OpenCL, new WebGPU kernels, expanded Hexagon op coverage, and scheduler improvements that avoid uploading unused inputs.
API changes
- Pruned deprecated API and removed the legacy DIAG_MASK_INF/DIAG_MASK_ZERO ops, bumping the RPC protocol to reject incompatible peers (llama/29801, llama/31946)
- Added ggml_rope_set_truncate/ggml_rope_get_truncate to control YaRN correction-bound rounding (llama/30206, llama/30802)
- Implemented the backward pass for TRI (llama/30712)
- Added MUL_MAT src1 precision tests and gating for ggml_prec_set_acc (llama/31896, llama/31851)
- Bumped the RPC protocol to v9 with faster loading and graceful failure on unreachable endpoints or failed handshakes (llama/29413, llama/30415)
Core changes
- Scheduler skips uploading inputs that are not read and prefetches only inputs produced by earlier splits (llama/31419, llama/32100)
- MoE cache can compute a share of the cache misses on the CPU and copy the results back asynchronously (llama/30966)
- Meta backend raises the compute view limit for buffers with few tensors (llama/31447)
Backend changes
CUDA
- Added few-row MMQ for batch sizes 2-24 and MMVF for BF16 few-row matmuls (llama/31533, llama/31959)
- Added OCP FP8 support and fused NVFP4 gate/up matmuls with GLU in MMQ (llama/28413, llama/31296)
- Extended FlashAttention with an sm70 head-size-256 config and MMA head sizes 40/72 (llama/27997, llama/30285)
- Improved graph handling: skip compat checks on reuse, re-instantiate on cluster-dim changes, move graph state (llama/32004, llama/31284, llama/32001)
- MoE: skip empty MMQ stream-k tiles, linearize the MoE layout, and sanitize post-bias NaNs (llama/32067, llama/31047, llama/31005)
- Added a debug buffer pool and halved the VMM pool reservation with reserve retries (llama/31919, llama/30542)
- HIP: use a fixed BLAS workspace and add an MFMA lightning indexer for CDNA2 (llama/31838, llama/29050)
- Added a d_state=64 SSM_SCAN fast path and made radix Top-K deterministic for ties (llama/31818, llama/31084)
Metal
- Fused MoE routing and kept fusable node groups inside a single command buffer (llama/31615, llama/31688)
- Made radix Top-K deterministic for ties, added mul_mm for 32<=K<64, and switched TRI to select (llama/31084, llama/30982, llama/30711)
- Fixed GROUP_NORM for ne03>1 and out-of-bounds accesses in the FA output and SOLVE_TRI kernels (llama/31852, llama/31662, llama/32103)
Vulkan
- Added an Intel FlashAttention prefill kernel (llama/29357)
- Added batched tensor copies, a test-fusion interface, and ReBAR detection (llama/31418, llama/30769, llama/31658)
- Enabled dequantized KV with CM2, YaRN truncation, RDNA3/4 large-tile split-K, and large coopmat matmul on newer AMD drivers (llama/31526, llama/30802, llama/30280, llama/31587)
- Added a tiled-transpose concat shader and FWHT kernels for block widths above 512 (llama/30591, llama/29772)
- Fixed MoltenVK out-of-bounds accesses, GROUP_NORM workgroup limits, and FA scratch sizing (llama/31890, llama/31930, llama/30487)
- Capped scalar FlashAttention at 8 rows for large heads on Qualcomm (llama/30829)
SYCL
- Added a device-side MoE scheduler (llama/30156)
- Made the oneDNN FA cache thread-safe and un-gated fused SDPA for Alchemist at head_dim=64 (llama/31138, llama/31574)
- Cached the device id and reject buffers that would exceed VRAM (llama/31126, llama/32013, llama/31285)
- Added exact rounding for CPY to Q4_1/Q5_1/Q8_0, strided CLAMP, and f16 SWIGLU_OAI (llama/31465, llama/31784, llama/30857)
- Fixed AOT for allocations above 4GB (llama/31873)
OpenCL
- Added decomposed Adreno FlashAttention and improved decode performance (llama/32046, llama/31633)
- Added q6_k tiled, q8_0, and f32/q5_k multi-column GEMV kernels and f32 MUL_MAT_ID (llama/31758, llama/30947, llama/31783)
- Added arange, non-contiguous sigmoid, repeat for f16/i32/i16/bf16, and DSV4 HC pre/post kernels (llama/31829, llama/31687, llama/31782, llama/31623)
- Enabled multi-column GEMV by default for Adreno X2 (llama/31694)
WebGPU
- Added batched tensor API support and returned maxBufferSize from get_max_size (llama/31473, llama/31348)
- Added GROUP_NORM, MEAN, COUNT_EQUAL, and PAD_REFLECT_1D kernels (llama/31490, llama/31591, llama/31578, llama/31877)
- Supported the YaRN truncation config (llama/30802)
Hexagon
- Added Q5_0/Q5_1 support and optimized conv_2d while adding conv_3d (llama/32094, llama/31814)
- Fused post-norm residual add into RMS_NORM_MUL and added set_tensor_n (llama/31822, llama/31744)
- Added automatic libhtp loading and fixed 64-bit FastRPC handle truncation (llama/31781, llama/30952)
- Fixed the host build with clang-cl on Windows ARM64 (llama/32011)
CPU
- Switched MUL_MAT to F32 src1 and accumulate FlashAttention V in F32 (llama/31854, llama/29810)
- Added SpacemiT GATED_DELTA_NET RVV and Q4_1 32x256 HP kernels and enabled IME2 MXFP4 repack (llama/31897, llama/31929, llama/31776)
- Enabled the 4x4 simd_gemm tile on ARM NEON and added bf16/q8_0 VXE to llamafile (llama/32128, llama/31866)
CANN
- Fail early when a buffer type is unsupported (llama/31270)
ZDNN
- Accept non-zdnn tensors, invalidate compute tensors after each op, and fix release backend lib detection (llama/31824, llama/31905)
OpenVINO
- Supported the YaRN truncation config (llama/30802)
More info

Ggml v1.0.0
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-11-14
02:28:29 UTC
11:28:29 KST

Repository navigation
Overview
ggml 1.0.0 prunes the deprecated public API and the legacy DIAG_MASK ops, adds configurable YaRN truncation and FP8 support, and brings broad performance work across backends: few-row quantized matmuls and MoE fusion on CUDA/Metal, a Vulkan prefill FlashAttention path, a device-side MoE scheduler on SYCL, decomposed Adreno FlashAttention in OpenCL, new WebGPU kernels, expanded Hexagon op coverage, and scheduler improvements that avoid uploading unused inputs.
API changes
- Pruned deprecated API and removed the legacy DIAG_MASK_INF/DIAG_MASK_ZERO ops, bumping the RPC protocol to reject incompatible peers (llama/29801, llama/31946)
- Added ggml_rope_set_truncate/ggml_rope_get_truncate to control YaRN correction-bound rounding (llama/30206, llama/30802)
- Implemented the backward pass for TRI (llama/30712)
- Added MUL_MAT src1 precision tests and gating for ggml_prec_set_acc (llama/31896, llama/31851)
- Bumped the RPC protocol to v9 with faster loading and graceful failure on unreachable endpoints or failed handshakes (llama/29413, llama/30415)
Core changes
- Scheduler skips uploading inputs that are not read and prefetches only inputs produced by earlier splits (llama/31419, llama/32100)
- MoE cache can compute a share of the cache misses on the CPU and copy the results back asynchronously (llama/30966)
- Meta backend raises the compute view limit for buffers with few tensors (llama/31447)
Backend changes
CUDA
- Added few-row MMQ for batch sizes 2-24 and MMVF for BF16 few-row matmuls (llama/31533, llama/31959)
- Added OCP FP8 support and fused NVFP4 gate/up matmuls with GLU in MMQ (llama/28413, llama/31296)
- Extended FlashAttention with an sm70 head-size-256 config and MMA head sizes 40/72 (llama/27997, llama/30285)
- Improved graph handling: skip compat checks on reuse, re-instantiate on cluster-dim changes, move graph state (llama/32004, llama/31284, llama/32001)
- MoE: skip empty MMQ stream-k tiles, linearize the MoE layout, and sanitize post-bias NaNs (llama/32067, llama/31047, llama/31005)
- Added a debug buffer pool and halved the VMM pool reservation with reserve retries (llama/31919, llama/30542)
- HIP: use a fixed BLAS workspace and add an MFMA lightning indexer for CDNA2 (llama/31838, llama/29050)
- Added a d_state=64 SSM_SCAN fast path and made radix Top-K deterministic for ties (llama/31818, llama/31084)
Metal
- Fused MoE routing and kept fusable node groups inside a single command buffer (llama/31615, llama/31688)
- Made radix Top-K deterministic for ties, added mul_mm for 32<=K<64, and switched TRI to select (llama/31084, llama/30982, llama/30711)
- Fixed GROUP_NORM for ne03>1 and out-of-bounds accesses in the FA output and SOLVE_TRI kernels (llama/31852, llama/31662, llama/32103)
Vulkan
- Added an Intel FlashAttention prefill kernel (llama/29357)
- Added batched tensor copies, a test-fusion interface, and ReBAR detection (llama/31418, llama/30769, llama/31658)
- Enabled dequantized KV with CM2, YaRN truncation, RDNA3/4 large-tile split-K, and large coopmat matmul on newer AMD drivers (llama/31526, llama/30802, llama/30280, llama/31587)
- Added a tiled-transpose concat shader and FWHT kernels for block widths above 512 (llama/30591, llama/29772)
- Fixed MoltenVK out-of-bounds accesses, GROUP_NORM workgroup limits, and FA scratch sizing (llama/31890, llama/31930, llama/30487)
- Capped scalar FlashAttention at 8 rows for large heads on Qualcomm (llama/30829)
SYCL
- Added a device-side MoE scheduler (llama/30156)
- Made the oneDNN FA cache thread-safe and un-gated fused SDPA for Alchemist at head_dim=64 (llama/31138, llama/31574)
- Cached the device id and reject buffers that would exceed VRAM (llama/31126, llama/32013, llama/31285)
- Added exact rounding for CPY to Q4_1/Q5_1/Q8_0, strided CLAMP, and f16 SWIGLU_OAI (llama/31465, llama/31784, llama/30857)
- Fixed AOT for allocations above 4GB (llama/31873)
OpenCL
- Added decomposed Adreno FlashAttention and improved decode performance (llama/32046, llama/31633)
- Added q6_k tiled, q8_0, and f32/q5_k multi-column GEMV kernels and f32 MUL_MAT_ID (llama/31758, llama/30947, llama/31783)
- Added arange, non-contiguous sigmoid, repeat for f16/i32/i16/bf16, and DSV4 HC pre/post kernels (llama/31829, llama/31687, llama/31782, llama/31623)
- Enabled multi-column GEMV by default for Adreno X2 (llama/31694)
WebGPU
- Added batched tensor API support and returned maxBufferSize from get_max_size (llama/31473, llama/31348)
- Added GROUP_NORM, MEAN, COUNT_EQUAL, and PAD_REFLECT_1D kernels (llama/31490, llama/31591, llama/31578, llama/31877)
- Supported the YaRN truncation config (llama/30802)
Hexagon
- Added Q5_0/Q5_1 support and optimized conv_2d while adding conv_3d (llama/32094, llama/31814)
- Fused post-norm residual add into RMS_NORM_MUL and added set_tensor_n (llama/31822, llama/31744)
- Added automatic libhtp loading and fixed 64-bit FastRPC handle truncation (llama/31781, llama/30952)
- Fixed the host build with clang-cl on Windows ARM64 (llama/32011)
CPU
- Switched MUL_MAT to F32 src1 and accumulate FlashAttention V in F32 (llama/31854, llama/29810)
- Added SpacemiT GATED_DELTA_NET RVV and Q4_1 32x256 HP kernels and enabled IME2 MXFP4 repack (llama/31897, llama/31929, llama/31776)
- Enabled the 4x4 simd_gemm tile on ARM NEON and added bf16/q8_0 VXE to llamafile (llama/32128, llama/31866)
CANN
- Fail early when a buffer type is unsupported (llama/31270)
ZDNN
- Accept non-zdnn tensors, invalidate compute tensors after each op, and fix release backend lib detection (llama/31824, llama/31905)
OpenVINO
- Supported the YaRN truncation config (llama/30802)
More info

Nvidia director sold nearly $1B in stock weeks before the Jensen Huang scandal
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-11-14
02:21:36 UTC
11:21:36 KST

Nvidia director sold nearly $1B in stock weeks before the Jensen Huang scandal broke — and no trading plan was flagged
Nvidia's second-largest shareholder sold about $946 million in company stock in the months leading up to CEO Jensen Huang's resignation on Nov. 12.
Nvidia [NASDAQ: NVDA] Board Director Mark Stevens was one of the top AI sellers in Q3 2026, selling roughly 4.2 million shares, according to filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission. There were three separate batches of stock sales from Stevens, who joined the Nvidia board in 2008 following an earlier stint as a director from 1993 to 2006.
Must Read
- Jeff Bezos backs a platform that lets anyone invest in rental homes for as little as $100 — 5 ways to build wealth like a landlord without actually being one
- Dave Ramsey warns nearly 50% of Americans are making 1 big Social Security mistake. Here's what it is and 3 simple steps to fix it ASAP
- A single line on your car insurance policy could be inflating your premium by up to 30% — here's what to change
The first common stock sale took place from Aug. 31 to Sept. 2 at equity prices ranging from $220 to $226, generating $411 million in new cash. The second sale stretched from Sept. 3 to Sept. 4 at prices ranging between $227 to $234 per share, garnering about $236 million. The third sale occurred on Sept. 18 at roughly $220 per share, netting roughly $300 million.
Still holding plenty of Nvidia stock
Prearranged trading plans are used by executives to buy or sell shares of their firm on specific dates or target prices. It's a mechanism to wall off company employees from insider trading accusations as long as they stick to the automatic plan.
The SEC first instituted the practice in 2000 and modified it in 2022 to include a 90-day waiting period for starting trades. In some cases, the plans were abused by executives in instances like executing share sales just before an earnings report.
In Stevens's case, he didn't have such a trading plan, but that's not necessarily a red flag on its own. Insiders cashing out of their stock will do so for a variety of reasons that aren't always tied to a company's performance, such as quickly raising liquidity. In Nvidia's case, the move could pour water on the enthusiasm of retail investors to buy into an AI titan that has also attracted short sellers.
The first two stock sales in late August and early September followed a robust Q2 earnings report that caused Nvidia shares to jump about 10% in valuein the following week. Stevens still holds about 27.5 million shares in Nvidia, a colossal position.

Security Agencies Worldwide Found to Use Ad-Based Surveillance System
An investigation by Bloomberg into Penlink’s ad-based surveillance system Webloc builds off Citizen Lab research, identifying additional customers of the tracking technology. The findings that Webloc has been acquired by security agencies in a number of countries aligns with potential customers we identified in our April report.
Senior researcher Wolfie Christl notes that Webloc “is a powerful mass surveillance tool that’s trickling down from military and intelligence agencies to federal law enforcement and then to state and local police.”
Our report used open source research, freedom of information requests, and server infrastructure mapping to identify Webloc customers in the US, El Salvador, and Hungary. Since then, the Austrian Ministry of the Interior has also been confirmed as a customer. The Bloomberg investigation identified customers in additional countries including the UK, Netherlands, Germany, Mexico, Singapore, Saudi Arabia, UAE, and Israel.
The lawfulness of using these systems in Europe and the UK is highly controversial. While intrusive and disproportionate ad-based mass surveillance is problematic everywhere, its use in authoritarian countries identified by reporting is particularly dangerous.

Elephants found to be increasingly isolated leading to fractured social networks
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-11-14
02:02:42 UTC
11:02:42 KST

Elephants Found to be Increasingly Isolated, Leading to Fractured Social Networks
With a troubling decline in the population, researchers warn of a tipping point for the highly social animals
Published Date
Article Content
Key Takeaways
- UC San Diego researchers studied the social dynamics of hundreds of Asian elephants over more than a decade in Sri Lanka.
- They tracked a decrease in the population of the highly social animals that has led to fractured and more isolated communities.
- Surpassing a social “tipping point,” they warn, can be detrimental to the future of the animals.
Humans and many other social animals thrive in well-established community networks. Asian elephants are one example of a species that flourishes in groups that work together to access food and care for their young, among other social bonds.
University of California San Diego scientists in the School of Biological Sciences studying the intricacies of Asian elephant community structures have documented a troubling downturn in the population of the animals resulting in fractured social communities. Their study is published on the cover of the November 12 issue of Science.
Analyzing the social dynamics of more than 440 wild female Asian elephants over 12 years at the Udawalawe National Park in Sri Lanka, the researchers studied key shifts in the demographics of the elephants that seemed to trigger social communities becoming smaller and more isolated.
“We found that gradual accumulation of losses from turnover preceded sudden change in the social networks among females in a wild population of Asian elephants,” the researchers explained in the study, which was led by Postdoctoral Researcher Anastasia Madsen from the laboratory of Associate Professor Shermin de Silva in the Department of Ecology, Behavior and Evolution. de Silva also serves as president and founder of the conservation nonprofit Trunks & Leaves Inc.
The researchers’ analysis indicates a social structure tipping point. As the number of elephants in the population decreased over time, due to a combination of likely deaths, permanent emigrations of elephants and fewer incoming individuals, the population as a whole appears to have crossed a critical threshold that resulted in a shift from large, densely connected social communities, to smaller and less-connected social groupings.
“We see individual elephants leaving and possibly dying at accelerating rates, but new individuals are not coming into the population,” said Madsen. “With fewer individuals in the population, those who are left will naturally have fewer relationships. However, the remaining elephants are also changing their relationships with each other.”
This new dynamic is a cause for concern, says Madsen, since the animals leverage their social groups and connections to forage, acquire information and raise young.
“We can probably all relate to the feeling of social isolation brought about, paradoxically, with the advent of digital communications that seem to remove the physical constraints of needing to be in the same place at the same time,” said de Silva. “But for many social species, which includes ourselves as much as elephants, we have to remember that social connectivity is very much a matter of sharing space and building relationships throughout our lives. Crucially, in order to have resilient communities, we need to be able to replace the relationships that are lost over time.”
Many elephant populations are already impacted through deaths resulting from poaching and conflicts with humans. Other contributing factors may be disruptions in habitat connectivity and less food available for the elephants as ecological conditions change across the 119-square-mile park and surroundings.
The new social fracturing structure observed by the scientists may not be easily repaired, the researchers warn.
“In general, we need to be more aware of these types of tipping points where we see sudden shifts after changes have been slowly building up,” said Madsen. “Once we move past the tipping point, it’s much harder to go back to previous states.”
The new findings will serve future studies seeking to understand shifts in animal society structures, how to detect such tranformations and the factors responsible for vulnerabilities. The study also stimulates ongoing discussions for conserving elephant populations as humans expand into areas where elephants historically thrived.
“We are gaining more evidence that studying social patterns is an important tool for us to see when things are going wrong in natural populations and, hopefully, to be able to do something about it,” said Madsen.
The researchers of the study were: Anastasia E. Madsen, T.V. Pushpakumara, U. Sameera Weerathunga, Devaka K. Weerakoon and Shermin de Silva.
Funding for the research was provided by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Asian Elephant Conservation Grants (F11AP00258, F14AP00256 and F17AP00308); National Science Foundation (grant DBI-2305860); University of Pennsylvania; UC San Diego; and Trunks & Leaves Inc.

GigChain Keys – a free, open-source MainStage alternative
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-11-14
01:47:30 UTC
10:47:30 KST

Download · Getting started · User guide · Get help · What's new · Discord · ♥ Sponsor
GigChain Keys is a live-performance host for keyboard players, in the spirit of MainStage and Gig Performer. It plays the VST3 and VST2 instruments and effects already on your computer, keeps every song of the night in a setlist with its own sounds, shows each song's chords and lyrics big enough to read from the keys, and turns those chords into notes falling onto a keyboard so you can practise them.
It is free, with no adverts, no licence keys and no nag screens. It is open source too, under the GPL.
Important
Public alpha: testers wanted. GigChain Keys is in early testing. It works and is played on real rigs, but it has not yet met the wide range of computers, audio interfaces, keyboards and plugins out there. Features and setlist files may still change between versions, and you may meet bugs. Please try it at home and in rehearsal before trusting it on a gig, keep copies of your setlists, and tell us what works and what breaks. Your feedback decides what gets fixed and built next.
All versions, with their release notes, are on the Releases page.
During the alpha, the Windows installer and the macOS app are not
code-signed. Code-signing certificates carry a yearly cost, and they will
be added as the project grows and community interest and
sponsorship make that possible. Until then, Windows
and macOS show a one-time warning on first start; the steps below get past
it. The builds are made from the source in this repository by its public
build scripts, and every release lists the SHA-256 checksum of each file
(SHA256SUMS.txt), so you can check your download is the genuine one:
Get-FileHash .\GigChainKeys-0.1.0-x64-setup.exe -Algorithm SHA256   # Windows (PowerShell)shasum -a 256 GigChainKeys-0.1.0-arm64.dmg                          # macOS (Terminal)
sha256sum GigChainKeys-0.6.0-x86_64.AppImage                         # Linux
AppImage: make it executable, then run it (or double-click it in your file manager):
chmod +x GigChainKeys-*-x86_64.AppImage
./GigChainKeys-*-x86_64.AppImage
(If it says "FUSE" is missing, install libfuse2, or run it with
--appimage-extract-and-run.)
.deb: sudo apt install ./gigchain-keys_*_amd64.deb, then start
GigChain Keys from your menu or type gigchain-keys. Remove it with
sudo apt remove gigchain-keys.
Sound goes through PulseAudio or PipeWire (or JACK, chosen in Settings;
on PipeWire, start the app with pw-jack to use JACK);
Linux VST3 plugins are found in ~/.vst3 and /usr/lib/vst3. The AppImage
uses your system's sound libraries: if it says libjack.so.0 is missing,
install libjack-jackd2-0 (the .deb installs it for you).
Windows SmartScreen may say "Windows protected your PC". Click More info, then Run anyway. This happens once.
The app is not notarized by Apple yet. Open the disk image, drag GigChain Keys to Applications, and open it once. When macOS refuses, go to System Settings → Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway.
- Instruments: four come built in (Saw Stack Pro, Piano Pro, Pads Pro and the SoundFont Player, below), and any VST3 or VST2 instruments and effects play too. GigChain Keys finds them in the usual plugin folders by itself. Want more? These free ones cover pianos, synths and pads: The app shows the same list (Help > Get free instruments). They are the makers' own downloads, not part of GigChain Keys.
- A MIDI keyboard (USB or a MIDI interface). A sustain pedal, knobs and pads are used when present.
- An audio interface is recommended for low latency (ASIO on Windows). Your computer's own sound works too.
  
  
Perform: the song plays along its parts; Next part and Loop part land on the bar line.
  
  
Right-click a fader, a pan knob or the master: MIDI Learn, then turn a knob on your keyboard.
  
  
  
Warm-ups: the finger for every note, then the score.
- Download and install GigChain Keys, then start it.
- Open Settings (top right) and choose your audio device and MIDI keyboard.
- Click New setlist, then + Song.
- Open the Instruments tab on the left and double-click an instrument. Play!
- Paste the song's chords into the Chart tab, then try Perform and Practice.
The Getting started page walks through it step by step. Inside the app, press F1 (or click Help) at any time.
Short videos, each showing one part of GigChain Keys (all of them):
- The overview: the whole app, start to finish
- Loop station · Chord charts and lyrics · The 10-minute warm-up
- Layers, splits and effects · Sounds on your pads
- Saw Stack Pro, the EDM synth · Piano Pro, the EDM piano
The user guide is built into the app (Help → User guide, or F1) and is also here on GitHub:
- Something not working? Start with Troubleshooting.
- Found a bug? Report it. The support page says what to include (and where the log file is).
- Have an idea? Suggest a feature.
- A security problem? Please report it privately: see SECURITY.md.
- Want to talk to other players? Join the Discord.
Come and join the Discord: ask how to set up a sound, share your rig and your setlists, tell us what's missing for your gigs, or just hang out with other keys players. If you know someone who'd use GigChain Keys, send them the link.
GigChain Keys is free and stays free: no adverts, no paid version, no keys. If it helps your gigs, a donation keeps it going. It pays for the time to fix and build things, and the first goal is code-signing certificates, so Windows and macOS install GigChain Keys without a warning.
One-off or monthly, any amount, through GitHub Sponsors. Thank you!
GigChain Keys uses numbered versions. Each release lists what is new and what was fixed in the changelog and on the Releases page.
What is coming next is in the roadmap: bundled free instruments, a tablet remote for the music stand, melody and intro practice, and more.
GigChain Keys is written in C++20 with Qt 6 (QML) and hosts plugins with the Steinberg VST3 SDK; audio and MIDI go through RtAudio and RtMidi.
- Building from source: Windows, Linux and macOS
- Contributing: how to send a fix, and the code rules
- Releasing: how a version is built and published
- Roadmap: what is coming next
Everyone taking part is expected to follow the code of conduct.
- riversongswgs-glitch: testing the releases and reporting with videos and logs, which shaped the Flow bar, Practice in time with the click, chord lengths, the big count-in and the chart editor's fixes
GigChain Keys is free software: you can share and change it under the terms of the GNU General Public License, version 3 or later (LICENSE).
It is built with:
- Qt (LGPL-3.0)
- the Steinberg VST3 SDK (MIT)
- the Steinberg ASIO SDK (GPL-3.0)
- RtAudio and RtMidi (MIT-style)
- FluidSynth (LGPL-2.1-or-later), which plays SoundFonts in the SoundFont Player
- effects ported from Vital (GPL-3.0) in Saw Stack Pro and Piano Pro
- Piano Pro's concert grand: Alexander Holm's Salamander Grand Piano (CC BY 3.0); its upright from Versilian Studios' VCSL (CC0); its Rhodes: Jeff Learman's jRhodes3d (samples CC BY-NC 4.0); its Wurlitzer, CP80 and Pianet: Greg Sullivan's E-Pianos (CC BY 3.0)
- Pads Pro's string section from Versilian Studios' VSCO 2 CE (CC0) and its piano from the Splendid Grand Piano (public domain)
The full notices ship with the app (THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt).
VST is a registered trademark of Steinberg Media Technologies GmbH. ASIO is a trademark of Steinberg Media Technologies GmbH. MainStage, Logic, Gig Performer, Kickstart, Korg M1, Rhodes and DX7 are trademarks of their owners; GigChain Keys is not affiliated with them.

FAA Orders Nationwide Ground Stop for All Aircraft
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-11-14
01:30:00 UTC
10:30:00 KST

FAA Lifts Nationwide Ground Stop for All Aircraft [UPDATE] (businessinsider.com) 70
			
		 	
				Longtime Slashdot readers cold fjord and sinij share news that the FAA grounded flights nationwide after a communications failure disrupted air traffic control centers across the country. By Friday evening, the outage had resulted in nearly 5,000 flight cancellations and roughly 10,000 delays, with no timeline for restoring normal operations. Rumors are swirling that this could be related to the FAA's newly deployed SMART AI system or Microsoft's recent global outage, but both the agency and Microsoft said they had no indication that their technology was responsible. Business Insider reports:  US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said just after 4:15 pm. Eastern time that the nationwide flight traffic halt came "following a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers." "FAA technicians are investigating the issue," he said in a post on X. The outage comes the same week as the FAA deployed SMART, a new AI tool to help air traffic control. ASI, the company that makes the SMART system for the FAA, said that Friday's issues weren't "based on or a result of the SMART system, any product of ASI or our integration with FAA and ATC."
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said in a press conference Friday, when asked if the AI system might be related to the outage: "That's what we're looking at." Microsoft, which faced massive issues across its services this week, also said that it had "no indication" the ground stop was related to any Microsoft services. Meanwhile, the FAA said that the ground stop was due to "extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety."  UPDATE 1:33 UTC: Secretary Mullin and Secretary Duffy are currently briefing members of the press on the issue.
UPDATE 1:46 UTC: The FAA has lifted the nationwide ground stop after more than four hours. Officials said the disruption appears to have stemmed from a network router issue that cascaded nationwide, with no evidence of a cyberattack or connection to Microsoft's recent outage. Airlines warned that disruptions could continue in Saturday.

Ukraine knocks out 36% of Russia's oil refining capacity in under two weeks
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-11-14
03:10:22 EET
10:10:22 KST

Ukrainian drones knock out 36% of Russia's oil refining capacity in under two weeks
Smoke is rising in Leningrad Oblast after the drone attack, Nov. 11, 2026 (Photo: Social Media/via REUTERS)
Ukrainian drone strikes knocked out 36% of Russia’s total oil refining capacity in less than two weeks, hitting at least nine major refineries between Oct. 30 and Nov. 11, defense manufacturer Fire Point reported on Nov. 12.
The combined annual processing capacity of the Russian plants hit over the past 13 days exceeds 120 million metric tons of crude oil—accounting for 36% of the aggressor state’s entire domestic oil refining capacity.
"In under two weeks, enterprises accounting for more than a third of Russia's total oil refining capacity came under strike," Fire Point noted.
Recent Strikes on Russian Refineries
On Nov. 6, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that in direct retaliation for Russian strikes against Ukraine’s energy grid, Kyiv would press forward with its campaign targeting the aggressor state's oil refining infrastructure.
On Nov. 7, long-range drones struck Saratov Oil Refinery. Two days later, on Nov. 9, Ukrainian forces hit Russia's second-largest processing facility — Kirishi Oil Refinery in Leningrad Oblast.
On Nov. 11, strike drones hit oil export terminals at the Baltic port of Ust-Luga, a vital maritime hub for Russian crude shipments.
According to Reuters, Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian refineries since late October 2026 have reduced Russia's operational refining capacity by roughly 30% and triggered acute fuel shortages across at least six Russian oblasts.
The military war may be swinging in our favor, but the information war continues.
Just as an army needs soldiers, so does a free society need its journalists to ensure that people have access to honest, trustworthy voices to understand the world around them.
For the past five years, The New Voice of Ukraine has been working tirelessly to push back against Russian narratives and defend democracy. But we cannot do it alone.

Hawaii DOT: All West Coast flights halted by SpaceX debris after FAA ground stop
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-11-14
01:09:52 UTC
10:09:52 KST

FAA lifts nationwide ground stop: What Hawaii travelers should know
Travelers should continue checking with their carriers.
HONOLULU (HawaiiNewsNow) - A nationwide Federal Aviation Administration ground stop that disrupted several domestic flights to and from Hawaiʻi was lifted at around 3:20 p.m. Friday.
The Hawaiʻi Department of Transportation said in an update that both the nationwide ground stop and a temporary pause for space debris had been lifted.
Delays may continue as airlines accommodate passengers from earlier flights, officials said.
RELATED POST: Flights halted at airports across US due to air traffic control communications problems, FAA says
Initial ground stop affected domestic travel
The FAA issued the ground stop following a communications issue affecting air traffic control centers. Flight disruptions had been intermittent with restrictions changing throughout the day.
Hawaiʻi Department of Transportation Director Ed Sniffen said officials were notified of the ground stop at about 10:50 a.m. for domestic flights to and from the continental U.S.
Interisland flights were not affected, he said.
“There’s been adjustments throughout. Initially, flights, international flights were unrestricted. Then we got notifications that there are some conflicts with the international flights,” Sniffen said.
At around 12:30 p.m., Sniffen said some flights had been cleared to leave Hawaiʻi for the West Coast.
Officials were repositioning aircraft and planning to use taxiways and some runways for parking to make room for arriving planes, he said.
SpaceX debris halted flights again
In a 1:55 p.m. update, the DOT announced all West Coast flights had been halted due to debris from a SpaceX launch.
SpaceX launched its Starship rocket from Texas on Friday, but its first-stage booster malfunctioned and ended up in the Gulf after an automatic abort, according to The Associated Press. The spacecraft continued toward orbit.
“The big message to all the public is things are changing pretty quickly,” Sniffen said. “Before you come down to the airport, make sure you reach out to your carrier.”
11/13/26 1:55PM: All west coast flights have been halted due to debris from SpaceX launch. Please continue to check with your carrier for further updates. https://t.co/Et1gtFbfe7
— Hawaii DOT (@DOTHawaii) November 13, 2026
What travelers should know
Hawaiian and Alaska airlines said a flexible travel policy was in place for guests who need to change their plans.
The airlines said it would take time to safely return operations to schedule after the ground stop was lifted.
Nationwide ground stops are rare. A pilot notification system outage prompted one in January 2023; the previous nationwide stop followed the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks.

SpaceX Falls Short of Historic Double Starship Catch
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-11-14
01:00:00 UTC
10:00:00 KST

SpaceX Falls Short of Historic Double Starship Catch (bakersfield.com) 22
			
		 	
				SpaceX's 15th Starship test flight successfully reached orbit Friday, but its historic attempt to catch both stages at the launch tower was derailed when the Super Heavy booster malfunctioned, forcing controllers to abort its return before it exploded after splashing down in the Gulf of Mexico. The upper-stage Starship did, however, successfully deploy 26 Starlink satellites and is scheduled to complete 15 orbits before attempting an unprecedented tower catch on Saturday. If successful, it would mark the first time a spacecraft has returned from orbit to land vertically at a launch tower. The Bakersfield Californian reports:  The original goal was to retrieve every single piece of the rocket for the purpose of future recycling, something yet to be achieved anywhere in the world. Musk sees this leading to the kind of fast and consistent launch rates necessary for building moon bases and sending people to Mars. Shortly after reaching orbit, Starship dropped off 26 of the company's most advanced Starlink satellites. The plan is for Starship to complete 15 laps around the world at an altitude of around 170 miles (275 kilometers) before heading back to the launch site for Saturday's grand finale.
SpaceX had already made three booster grabs at the company's sprawling Starbase near the U.S.-Mexico border. That made Friday's miss all the more surprising. "Well, that certainly isn't the news that we had hoped to hear for today," observed SpaceX launch commentator Kate Tice, adding that it was in line with the many rigorous safety checks to protect the pad. No explanation was provided for what went wrong. This was the first attempt to capture the upgraded version of the booster that stretches 236 feet (72 meters) -- the production model for moon and Mars expeditions. It will also be the first time the company attempts to catch the spacecraft, which spans 171 feet (52 meters). Together, they form the world's biggest and most powerful rocket -- an astounding 407 feet (124 meters) in height.
The spacecraft portion of the 14 previous Starships ended up in the ocean, either by design at flight's end or by accident in a stream of flaming wreckage. During the first full-scale test flight in 2023, multiple engines failed to ignite and the tumbling rocket's self-destruct system was activated. The last test, in September, was the first to reach orbit, but SpaceX did not try to recover any of the rocket stages. You can watch a recorded livestream of the launch on YouTube.

Amtrak booking system experiencing major issues amid nationwide FAA ground stop

09:52:29 KST

Amtrak booking system returns to normal after outage during nationwide FAA ground stop
WASHINGTON - Amtrak said its booking system is returning to normal after a network outage that coincided with a nationwide FAA ground stop.
Users report outage
What we know:
Users on social media started sharing frustrations over ticket reservations Friday afternoon, with travelers showing error messages on Amtrak's website and app.
Hundreds of users reported issues on DownDetector, beginning shortly before 5 p.m. Friday, with another surge just before 6 p.m.
Issues caused by increased demand
What they're saying:
In response to a request for comment, Amtrak's Communications Director W. Kyle Anderson said that "Amtrak service is operating normally, and we are seeing increased demand for travel across our network."
Responding to a frustrated customer Friday, Amtrak officials said in a post on X that the booking issues were related to a system-wide update, but did not elaborate.
Around 9 p.m. officials said the booking systems were returning to normal.
The company said some customers may still experience issues while processing payments, booking trips or modifying existing reservations. Amtrak’s call centers experienced higher-than-normal call volumes, resulting in longer wait times for some.
FOX 5 DC attempted to call the support number during the outage, around 8 p.m., but an automated message said officials were unable to take calls due to "unusually high call volume."
Travelers scrambling during ground stop
The backstory:
The outage came as thousands of travelers across the country scrambled for new plans, after the Federal Aviation Administration issued a nationwide ground stop — the first since January 2023 and just the second since the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks.
The FAA has said that the ground stop was ordered due to a "temporary telecommunications outage." It has since been lifted.
The Source: Information in this story is from social media posts commenting on the ticket booking outage, error messages on Amtrak's website and app, phone calls to Amtrak's support and media relations lines and previous FOX reporting on the Federal Aviation Administration's nationwide ground stop.

Anthropic Upgrades Claude Code Projects to Run Parallel AI Workers Hands-Free
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-11-14
00:28:11 UTC
09:28:11 KST

Anthropic Upgrades Claude Code Projects to Run Parallel AI Workers Hands-Free
Anthropic ships a proactive coordinator, shareable read-only threads, reminders, and /btw and /fork slash commands to Claude Code Projects.
- Claude Code Projects coordinator is now proactive, answering questions and pushing thread status updates in chat.
- Individual threads can be shared as read-only links to signed-in Claude users; threads with local computer access are excluded.
- Reminders let a thread hide itself and resurface in the project chat at a scheduled time.
- /btw opens a side thread for tangents; /fork branches a new thread from the current one.
- Threads panel adds a recents row and artifact thumbnails for easier retrieval across large projects.
- Public beta on Pro and Max across web, desktop, and the latest mobile app; Team and Enterprise excluded.
Anthropic has updated Claude Code Projects with proactive coordinator messages, read-only thread sharing, reminders, branching commands, and improved artifact navigation. The changes reduce the monitoring required when several cloud sessions work in parallel.
Each project is a long-running conversation with a coordinator that assigns work to threads. Every thread runs as an independent Claude Code cloud session with its own repository copy and Git branch. The coordinator directs the project from thread reports, while overlapping code changes surface as standard Git merge conflicts when branches are combined.
The coordinator reports without prompting
The coordinator now answers questions directly in project chat and posts status updates as threads progress. Previously, developers had to monitor the thread list to find sessions waiting for input. The updated behavior brings pending decisions, completed tasks, and blocked work into the main conversation.
Read-only links stop at local access
Individual threads can now be shared through read-only links with anyone signed in to Claude. A developer can open the thread menu, select Share, and send the generated URL without exposing the rest of the project.
Threads that accessed a local computer remain unshareable. The restriction prevents shared transcripts from exposing local file contents, shell output, or other machine data gathered during the session.
Park a thread or branch the work
The two slash commands were already available in regular Claude Code sessions. Their addition to Projects brings the same branching workflow to coordinated, multi-thread work.
Artifacts surface sooner
The threads panel now places recently opened, updated, and pinned threads in a row at the top. Each thread can also display thumbnails for generated documents, diagrams, and other artifacts, with the previews controlled through view settings.
The redesign simplifies project settings and local-folder access as well. Anthropic has released the changes on the web, desktop clients, and the latest mobile app.
Parallelism draws from the same allowance
Anthropic introduced the public beta on September 17 for Pro and Max subscribers who joined the waitlist. Team and Enterprise plans remain unsupported. Eligible subscribers who lack access can still join the waitlist.
Projects carry no separate fee, but every worker consumes the subscriber’s existing Claude Code allowance. Anthropic limits accounts to 200 new threads per day across all projects. A thread that reaches a usage limit pauses and resumes automatically when capacity becomes available.
Project usage appears separately in the usage controls, and developers can choose the model and effort level for the coordinator and worker threads. New projects default to Opus for both roles, with low effort for the coordinator and high effort for workers. Several high-effort sessions running at once can exhaust plan limits faster than a single Claude Code session.
Where many threads pay off
Projects fit engineering work that can be divided into independent tasks and reconciled through branches and pull requests. Anthropic’s examples include:
- Performance work: Assign separate threads to profile endpoints, test optimizations, and open pull requests. A target such as p75 checkout latency refers to the response time at or below which 75% of requests finish.
- Cross-repository migrations: Connect API, web, and mobile repositories, then create one thread per codebase and report the required merge order.
- Batch changes: Distribute refactors, dependency upgrades, test repairs, or bug-triage items across parallel sessions.
Tasks with strict dependencies still require developers to sequence pull requests and resolve conflicts. Projects also remain cloud-only and limited to Claude Code, while parallel workers draw from the same plan limits. Small changes that fit one branch and one context window generally consume fewer resources in a regular Claude Code session.
